Squaring coordinates gives a three-strategy antisymmetric replicator with conserved u+v+w and H=u^c v^b w^a; the positive simplex has strictly concave log H and a single interior center, so each regular level is a simple periodic orbit. The physical-time visits to the three corners have divergent parts L/(2ab), L/(2ac) and L/(2bc), from integrating log-coordinate derivatives and bounded-integral residuals, while connecting arcs stay O(1). Uniform spherical-area sampling pushes (u,v,w) to Dirichlet(1/2,1/2,1/2), so E H^{-q} is finite precisely for q<1/(2 max(a,b,c)), including divergence at equality. T= S/(2abc) log(1/H)+O(1) transfers this to the stated tail and sharp moment cutoff.
